**Finding submitted: `missing` (critical rule IP), confidence 0.82**

**What the document does and doesn't say:**
- **Section 2(d)** (p0029) is a one-sided ownership clause: TrueLink retains all ownership in the Interface. That alone is acceptable under the playbook — a vendor keeping its platform is fine.
- **No counterpart for us.** There is no ownership or assignment provision covering the Support Services work product produced by TrueLink's programmer under Section 4.
- **"Client Content" and "Client's Intellectual Property" are defined** (p0011, p0012) but are only ever used as confidentiality hooks (Sections 8(e), 10(b), 10(c)) — never to confirm title.
- **Section 8(d)** (p0054) grants TrueLink a worldwide right to "use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit... and store Credit Data" (borrower/loan applicant data), with no statement that ownership stays with us. That is a live risk given the walk-away position on Customer Data.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** a single new Section 2(e) inserted after p0029 that (i) assigns Support Services results and other deliverables to us, excluding the Interface and TrueLink IP; (ii) grants a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to any TrueLink IP embedded in those deliverables; (iii) confirms we retain all rights in Client Content, Client IP and borrower/loan/customer data, and that the Section 8(d) licence conveys no ownership; and (iv) excludes joint ownership.

The comment offers the fallback (TrueLink keeps title to generic tools, we take a perpetual, sublicensable licence to the deliverables) so the negotiation has an obvious landing zone.
